title: How to get more out of every solar battery charge (without adding panels)
summary: Discover how to enhance your solar battery's performance and save money with Enphase's innovative PowerMatch technology.
body_markdown:
You invested in solar panels and a home battery to lower your bills and keep the lights on when the grid goes down. So why does it feel like your battery drains faster than it should—even on days when you barely use any power?


The answer isn't your panels. It isn't even your battery's capacity. It's something happening quietly inside your system, every single hour of every day, whether you're home or not.


It's called **tare loss—** energy consumed by the battery system itself to operate and convert power rather than being delivered to your home. Once you understand it, you'll see why reducing these losses can help you get more usable energy from your battery.


## Your battery is working even when your home isn't


Your solar battery doesn't just store energy— the battery system also uses some energy to operate its electronics and convert stored energy into power your home can use, even when your home is using very little electricity.


Think of a car left idling in your driveway. Engine running, fuel burning—going nowhere.


Many battery systems use a single centralized hybrid inverter that remains active even when your home is using very little power. At low power demand, some hybrid string‑inverter systems can operate at significantly lower efficiency. For example, some systems can operate at around 55% efficiency when powering low loads.


Unlike these systems, microinverter technology can ramp power up or down based on demand, and even shut down individual microinverters when they aren't needed. This helps reduce energy losses during periods of low power demand.


According to Enphase data from real U.S. homes, that inverter is burning standby energy for over **17 hours every day** , even when your home barely needs it. Over months and years, that's real money quietly disappearing.


## There's now a smarter way to manage battery power


The Enphase IQ Battery 10C is designed from the ground up to solve this problem, and it does it through a technology called[PowerMatch](https://enphase.com/homeowners/home-solar-batteries/powermatch) .


Unlike many conventional battery systems, the IQ Battery 10C doesn't rely on one large centralized inverter. Instead, it has four independent built-in microinverters. This distributed architecture is the foundation that makes PowerMatch work.


## Here's what happens in practice:


PowerMatch monitors your home's power demand and activates only the number of microinverters needed to meet that demand. When demand is low, fewer microinverters operate. As your home's usage increases, additional microinverters activate.


It's the same logic as start-stop technology in a modern car — when full power isn't needed, the system reduces what's operating, then brings more capacity online as demand increases.


**The result:** less energy lost during low-load


operation, and more of the energy you actually stored available to power your home.


## What the difference looks like in real terms


This isn't a marginal improvement. The numbers are significant:


**What you gain** **How much**


Extra usable energy daily Up to 1 kWh per day vs. certain hybrid string-inverter battery systems*


That's equivalent to... Running your refrigerator for a full 24 hours


Savings over battery life (1 unit) Up to $2,000 in potential additional savings over 15 years*


Savings over battery life (2 units) Up to $6,000 over 15 years*


*Based on $0.37/kWh


([PG&E California residential rates](https://www.pge.com/assets/pge/docs/account/rate-plans/residential-electric-rate-plan-pricing.pdf) ). Actual savings vary by usage, location, and utility rate.


That 1 kWh per day doesn't sound like much—but multiply it across 365 days a year, factor in rising utility rates, and it represents a meaningful chunk of the total return on your battery investment. And if you ever add a second battery, the potential savings can increase, although the actual benefit depends on system configuration and energy use.


## No new hardware. No installer visit.


One of the most important things about PowerMatch: you don't need to buy anything new to get it.


PowerMatch is delivered as a **software update** through the[Enphase platform](https://enphase.com/homeowners/enphase-app) . If you already have a compatible system, it can be enabled without any hardware changes or a visit from an installer. As Enphase's senior[VP Aaron Gordon](https://investor.enphase.com/news-releases/news-release-details/enphase-energy-expands-powermatch-technology-north-america) puts it: "Software can make the hardware better over time."


PowerMatch is available for:


- **IQ Battery 10C** — across the United States and Puerto Rico
- **IQ Battery 5P** — across the United States, Puerto Rico, Canada, Mexico, Bermuda, Cayman Islands, Bahamas, and Panama


The IQ Battery 10C itself is built on lithium iron phosphate (LFP) chemistry, has been tested to UL 9540A, supports whole-home backup when configured with compatible Enphase equipment, including the IQ Meter Collar, and carries a 15-year limited warranty covering 6,000 cycles.


## Making your solar investment work harder


Most homeowners buy a battery for one of two reasons: to cut their electricity bills, or to keep the house running when the grid fails. PowerMatch helps you get more usable energy from your battery during everyday operation.


Every[kilowatt-hour](https://enphase.com/blog/homeowners/how-many-kwh-does-average-us-home-use) you recover from tare loss is energy that can instead be available to power your home rather than being consumed by the battery system. With electricity rates climbing in states across the US, recovering even 1 kWh per day has a compounding effect on your payback period and lifetime savings.


This is also a glimpse at where[home energy storage](https://enphase.com/homeowners/home-solar-batteries) is heading: away from static, one‑size-fits-all hardware, and toward intelligent systems that optimize themselves automatically—getting better the longer you own them, not worse.
